title: Command Execution and Unsafe Reflection
platform_conditions: Java SE 8+ standard library (java.lang.Runtime, java.lang.ProcessBuilder, java.lang.Class); applies on all target operating systems
security_mechanism: Runtime.getRuntime().exec(String) tokenizes the command with StringTokenizer on whitespace, so a single-string form splits arguments unpredictably, and any form that routes through a shell ('sh', '-c', concatenated) hands the whole string to shell interpretation, where ';', '|', and '$(...)' start attacker commands. Class.forName(name) plus Method.invoke turns a name from input into arbitrary class loading and method invocation in-process, and URLClassLoader with an attacker-influenced URL loads classes from a remote codebase directly.

source_sink_clues.source: Request fields used as command strings or arguments, class/method names from input resolved via reflection, and codebase URLs from config or requests.
source_sink_clues.sink: Runtime.exec / ProcessBuilder.start with shell-composed strings; Class.forName with a dynamic name followed by reflection; URLClassLoader with attacker-influenced URLs

tracking_guards: Require ProcessBuilder with a fixed executable and an argument list where each dynamic value is one element (no shell, no concatenated single string); require reflection targets be resolved from a compiled-in allowlist mapping rather than from input; require any classloader URL come from validated internal locations.
not_candidate_when: The command is a fixed executable with input as a single argv element and no shell involvement, reflected class names come from a fixed allowlist, the classloader loads only from the application's own sealed artifacts, or the input is validated to a grammar that cannot contain whitespace, shell metacharacters, or option prefixes.
synthetic_safe_example: ProcessBuilder pb = new ProcessBuilder("/bin/safe", arg); pb.start();
public_references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
CWE-470: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/470.html
